title: fix(xtask): CP00 proof-level check has no polarity on the PR side, so a correct Claim Boundary arms it
body:
`semantic-close-containment`'s `CP00-PROOF-LEVEL-CONTRADICTION` fires on PRs that exclude nothing. Found on PR #15621, which it flags on every run.

## Root cause: polarity is applied to one side only

`proof_level_is_explicitly_excluded` (`xtask/src/bin/semantic-close-containment.rs:1137`):

```rust
PROOF_LEVEL_TERMS.iter().any(|term| {
    issue_requires_proof_level_term(&issue_requirements, term)   // clause-scoped polarity
        && contains_proof_level_term(&exclusions_lower, term)    // bare word presence
})
```

The **issue** side runs the full polarity machinery — `requirement_units` → `unit_requires_proof_level_term` → `term_local_requirement` → `nearest_polarity_signal`, with 21 negative-polarity markers and 6 requirement predicates, scoped per clause.

The **PR** side is `contains_proof_level_term`, which is `contains_word`. No polarity, no clause scoping, no distinction between asserting a proof level and disclaiming it.

So any occurrence of `installed` / `public` / `packaged` / `presentation` / `release` / `actual host` anywhere in the PR's **Claim Boundary or Non-goals** counts as excluding that proof level — including a sentence that *proves* it.

## Reproduction (PR #15621 against #7129)

Three predicates, all true, none of them evidence of an exclusion:

| Predicate | Why it is true |
|---|---|
| `contains_explicit_exclusion(pr)` | the Claim Boundary contains **"Not claimed:"**, one of the eight markers |
| `contains_proof_level_term(pr, "public")` | the Claim Boundary says *"**Provably true:** no **public** formatter surface … offers `compat` as an engine"* — an assertion that the public surface **is** covered |
| `issue_requires_proof_level_term(issue, "public")` | #7129's Objective says "remove compat from **public** configuration" |

The sentence that arms the rule is the strongest positive claim in the PR.

## Why this is structural, not one unlucky PR

The repository's own `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` asks for:

```
## Claim Boundary
<!-- Keep the conclusion inside the proof boundary. What becomes provably true,
     and what is explicitly out of scope? -->
```

`explicitly out of scope` is itself one of the eight exclusion markers, and the section exists precisely to state what is and isn't proven. A PR that fills the template in well, states a precise boundary, and closes an issue whose acceptance mentions a public/installed/released surface will arm CP00 by construction — and the remedy the check proposes (`Advances` instead of `Closes`) is wrong whenever the acceptance criteria are in fact met.

The incentive is backwards: the cheapest way to clear the check is to delete the word "public" from the Claim Boundary, making the PR body vaguer.

## Suggested fix

Apply the polarity analysis that already exists to the PR side:

```rust
&& proof_level_term_is_excluded(&exclusions_lower, term)
```

where `proof_level_term_is_excluded` reuses `term_local_requirement`'s clause scoping, counting a term only when its nearest polarity signal marks it as *out of scope / not proven*, not when it appears in an assertion of coverage. `nearest_polarity_signal`, `proof_level_term_indices`, and the segment splitting are already written and tested; this is mostly wiring the existing helper to the other operand.

The existing `proof_level_polarity_*` unit tests only vary the **issue** body (`proof_level_from_bodies(issue, &excluding_pr("Public"))`), which is why the PR-side gap is not covered.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A Claim Boundary that *asserts* a public/installed/packaged/released surface is covered does not arm CP00.
- [ ] A Claim Boundary that genuinely disclaims one still arms it (negative control).
- [ ] A test varies the **PR** body with the issue fixed, mirroring the existing issue-side polarity tests.
- [ ] A PR filling in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`'s Claim Boundary as written does not arm the rule merely by using the template's vocabulary.

## Not in scope

Whether #15621 should say `Closes` or `Advances` — its acceptance criteria are met on inventory, and that is argued on the PR itself. This issue is only about the check arming on text that excludes nothing.

Related: PR #15621, #7129.
